title: Professions
bigQuestion: How are jobs changing, and why are all jobs important?
summary: Students learn words for new technology and space jobs and for emergency services, tell stories with the Simple Past and Past Progressive, describe people and things with who / which / that, and make open and closed compound nouns.
warmup: What do you want to be when you grow up? Why?
Which jobs help people in an emergency?
Would you like to travel into space? What would you do there?
Can you name a job that did not exist 50 years ago?
Who works hard to help people in your neighborhood?

grammar.title: Simple Past and Past Progressive
grammar.rule: Use the Past Progressive (was / were + -ing) for a longer action that was in progress in the past. Use the Simple Past for a short action that happened in the middle of it. We often join them with when or while.
grammar.form: I / he / she / it + was + verb-ing · you / we / they + were + verb-ing · ... when + Simple Past · while + Past Progressive
examples: We were driving to Abha when Grandma sent us a video message.
The phone rang while I was doing my homework.
Nouf wasn't sleeping when the fire truck went past.
What were you doing at seven o'clock last night?

items.prompt: Omar ___ a video message when the lights went out.
items.explanation: Recording was the longer action in the past, and Omar is one person, so we use was + -ing.

items.prompt: While the astronauts were sleeping, the satellite ___ a photo of Earth.
items.explanation: Taking a photo is the short action, so we use the Simple Past: took.

items.prompt: What ___ you doing at eight o'clock last night?
items.explanation: Questions in the Past Progressive use were with you: What were you doing?

items.prompt: The firefighters ___ dinner when the alarm rang.
items.explanation: Firefighters is plural, so we use were + -ing for the longer past action.

items.prompt: Sara ___ a fire truck while she was walking to school.
items.explanation: Seeing the truck is the short action, so we use the Simple Past: saw.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: I was reading when the phone rang.
I was read when the phone rang.
I reading when the phone was ring.
items.answer: I was reading when the phone rang.
items.explanation: The longer action uses was + -ing, and the short action uses the Simple Past.

items.prompt: ___ Khalid playing football when it started to rain?
items.explanation: For a Past Progressive question about one person, start with Was.

items.prompt: We ___ to Abha when Grandma called us.
items.explanation: We is plural, so the longer action is were + traveling.

items.prompt: Nouf ___ her homework when her brother came home.
items.explanation: Doing homework was in progress when her brother came, so we use was doing.

items.prompt: While the doctors were talking, the ambulance suddenly ___.
items.explanation: Suddenly tells us it is a short action, so we use the Simple Past: arrived.

items.prompt: Reem ___ TV when I called her. She was reading a book.
items.explanation: The negative of the Past Progressive is wasn't / was not + -ing.

items.prompt: ___ they playing outside when the storm started?
items.explanation: They is plural, so the question starts with Were.

items.prompt: The robotics engineer ___ a new robot when she had a great idea.
items.explanation: Designing was the longer action, and the idea came in the middle of it.

items.prompt: The police officer found the missing cat while he ___ in the park.
items.explanation: After while we usually use the Past Progressive for the longer action.

items.prompt: I ___ my leg while I was riding my bike.
items.explanation: Hurting your leg is a short action, and hurt is irregular: hurt - hurt.

items.answer: What were you doing at nine o'clock?
items.explanation: Question order: What + were + you + verb-ing.

items.answer: The phone rang while I was sleeping.
alt: While I was sleeping the phone rang.
items.explanation: While goes before the longer action: while I was sleeping.

items.answer: They were not watching the rocket.
items.explanation: Negative: were + not + verb-ing.

items.answer: Was your sister sleeping when you came home?
items.explanation: Past Progressive question: Was + person + verb-ing.

items.answer: The firefighters were washing the fire truck.
items.explanation: Plural subject + were + verb-ing.

items.prompt: Sara was cooking. The fire alarm rang.
answer: Sara was cooking when the fire alarm rang.
When the fire alarm rang, Sara was cooking.
When the fire alarm rang Sara was cooking.
items.explanation: When goes before the short action in the Simple Past.

items.prompt: The police officer found the missing bag. He was walking home.
answer: The police officer found the missing bag while he was walking home.
While he was walking home, the police officer found the missing bag.
While he was walking home the police officer found the missing bag.
items.explanation: While goes before the longer action in the Past Progressive.

items.prompt: They were watching the rocket launch.
answer: They were not watching the rocket launch.
They weren't watching the rocket launch.
items.explanation: Add not after were: were not / weren't + -ing.

items.prompt: Omar was talking to the astronaut.
answer: Was Omar talking to the astronaut?
items.explanation: Move was to the start of the sentence to make a question.

items.sentence: I was watching TV when my dad was come home.
items.answer: I was watching TV when my dad came home.
items.explanation: The short action needs the Simple Past: came, not was come.

items.sentence: They was playing in the garden.
items.answer: They were playing in the garden.
items.explanation: With they we use were, not was.

items.sentence: While Reem was reading, the lights went out.
items.answer: While Reem was reading, the lights went out.
items.explanation: Correct: was reading is the longer action and went out is the short action.

items.sentence: What did you doing when the ambulance arrived?
items.answer: What were you doing when the ambulance arrived?
items.explanation: The Past Progressive question uses were + -ing, not did + -ing.

grammar.title: Relative clauses with who, which, that
grammar.rule: We use who, which or that to say exactly which person or thing we mean. Use who for people and which for things or animals. That is fine for both people and things.
grammar.form: person + who / that + verb ... · thing / animal + which / that + verb ...
examples: The firefighter who saved the cat works at our fire station.
This is the rocket which flew to the space station.
I know a girl that wants to be an astronaut.
The video message that Grandpa sent was very funny.

items.prompt: An astronaut is a person ___ travels into space.
items.explanation: An astronaut is a person, so we use who.

items.prompt: A fire truck is a vehicle ___ carries water and ladders.
items.explanation: A fire truck is a thing, so we use which.

items.prompt: The man ___ saved the cat is a firefighter.
items.explanation: The man is a person, so we use who.

items.prompt: This is the satellite ___ sends photos of Earth.
items.explanation: That can be used for things like a satellite.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: The girl who won the prize is my sister.
The girl which won the prize is my sister.
The girl who she won the prize is my sister.
items.answer: The girl who won the prize is my sister.
items.explanation: Use who for a person, and don't add she after who.

items.prompt: I like robots ___ can talk to people.
items.explanation: Robots are things, so we use that (or which), not who.

items.prompt: The dog ___ was missing is now at home.
items.explanation: For animals we use which or that.

items.prompt: A cybersecurity analyst is someone ___ protects computers.
items.explanation: Someone is a person, so we use who (or that).

items.prompt: The rocket ___ we saw on TV was very tall.
items.explanation: A rocket is a thing, so we use which (or that).

items.prompt: Do you know the woman ___ is talking to the police officer?
items.explanation: The woman is a person, so we use who (or that).

items.prompt: The ambulance ___ came to our street was very fast.
items.explanation: An ambulance is a thing, so we use which (or that).

items.prompt: The boy ___ lost his bag went to the police station.
items.explanation: The boy is a person, so we use who (or that).

items.prompt: This is the video message ___ my uncle sent from NEOM.
items.explanation: A video message is a thing, so we use which (or that).

items.prompt: Robotics engineers are people ___ design and build robots.
items.explanation: People need who (or that).

items.answer: The man who fixes computers is my uncle.
alt: My uncle is the man who fixes computers.
items.explanation: Who fixes computers comes right after the man to tell us which man.

items.answer: This is the rocket that went to space.
items.explanation: That went to space tells us which rocket.

items.answer: I have a robot which can clean the floor.
items.explanation: Which can clean the floor comes right after a robot.

items.answer: She is the doctor who works at the hospital.
items.explanation: Who works at the hospital tells us which doctor.

items.answer: Is this the fire truck that you saw?
items.explanation: That you saw comes after the fire truck to tell us which one.

items.prompt: The firefighter is very brave. He saved the cat.
answer: The firefighter who saved the cat is very brave.
items.explanation: Put who saved the cat right after the firefighter. Don't repeat he.

items.prompt: I watched a video. It was about planets.
answer: I watched a video which was about planets.
items.explanation: Which replaces it, so we don't say it again.

items.prompt: Nouf has an aunt. She is an AI specialist.
answer: Nouf has an aunt who is an AI specialist.
items.explanation: Who replaces she, so we don't say she again.

items.prompt: This is the satellite. It takes photos of the weather.
answer: This is the satellite that takes photos of the weather.
items.explanation: That replaces it and tells us which satellite.

items.sentence: The police officer which helped me was kind.
items.answer: The police officer who helped me was kind.
items.explanation: A police officer is a person, so use who (or that), not which.

items.sentence: The rocket who flew to the moon was huge.
items.answer: The rocket which flew to the moon was huge.
items.explanation: A rocket is a thing, so use which (or that), not who.

items.sentence: I know a girl who wants to be an astronaut.
items.answer: I know a girl who wants to be an astronaut.
items.explanation: Correct: a girl is a person, so who is right.

items.sentence: The man who he works at the fire station is my neighbor.
items.answer: The man who works at the fire station is my neighbor.
items.explanation: Who already means the man, so we don't add he.

reading.title: A Surprise in Class
reading.text:
On Monday morning, Sara's class at her girls' school was having a science lesson. The students were drawing planets when someone knocked on the door. Their teacher, Ms. Amal, smiled. "We have a special visitor today," she said.

A woman in a blue jacket came in. "Hello, everyone. I'm Dr. Huda, and I'm a robotics engineer," she said. The students were very excited. Dr. Huda showed them a photo of a robot which works on a satellite. "My team designed this robot. It fixes small problems while the satellite is flying around Earth," she explained.

Sara put up her hand. "Is your job difficult?" she asked.

"Sometimes," said Dr. Huda. "Last year, we were testing the robot when it suddenly stopped. We worked all night, and we found the problem. Every job needs hard work and teamwork."

At the end of the lesson, Dr. Huda played a video message from an astronaut who was living on the space station. Sara felt proud and happy. That evening, she told her mother, "I want to be a robotics engineer too!"

questions.prompt: What were the students doing when the visitor knocked?
questions.explanation: The story says they were drawing planets when someone knocked.

questions.prompt: What is Dr. Huda's job?
questions.explanation: She says, "I'm a robotics engineer."

questions.statement: The robot in the photo works on a satellite.
questions.explanation: Dr. Huda showed a robot which works on a satellite.

questions.statement: The robot never had any problems.
questions.explanation: The robot suddenly stopped while they were testing it.

questions.prompt: Dr. Huda says every job needs hard work and ___.
questions.explanation: She says, "Every job needs hard work and teamwork."

questions.prompt: How did Sara feel at the end?
questions.explanation: The story says Sara felt proud and happy.

reading.title: The Missing Kitten
reading.text:
Hi, I'm Reem! Something exciting happened to my family last week, and I want to tell you about it.

On Thursday evening, my little brother Omar was crying because his kitten, Lulu, was missing. We looked everywhere in the house and in the garden. Then, while I was looking out of the window, I heard a tiny "meow". Lulu was at the top of a very tall palm tree!

My dad called the fire station. Ten minutes later, a big red fire truck stopped in front of our house. A firefighter who was very tall climbed a ladder. Everyone was watching quietly. He was holding a towel, and he wrapped Lulu in it very gently. When he came down, all our neighbors clapped.

The next day, Omar recorded a video message for the firefighters. He said, "Thank you for saving Lulu! You are heroes!" The firefighters sent a message back with a photo of the fire truck.

Now I understand that firefighters don't only stop fires. They help people and animals every day. I think their job is one of the most important jobs in our city.

questions.prompt: Why was Omar crying?
questions.explanation: Omar was crying because Lulu was missing.

questions.prompt: Where was Lulu?
options: at the top of a palm tree
questions.answer: at the top of a palm tree
questions.explanation: Reem saw Lulu at the top of a very tall palm tree.

questions.statement: Reem's dad called the police station.
questions.explanation: He called the fire station, not the police station.

questions.prompt: The firefighter wrapped Lulu in a ___.
questions.explanation: He was holding a towel and wrapped Lulu in it.

questions.statement: Omar sent a video message to say thank you.
questions.explanation: Omar recorded a video message for the firefighters.

questions.prompt: What does Reem think about firefighters now?
questions.explanation: She thinks it is one of the most important jobs in the city.

reading.title: Mom Saves the Website
reading.text:
Tuesday, March 14

Dear Diary,

Today was a strange day! I was doing my math homework after school when Uncle Khalid called. He has a small business which sells dates and coffee online. He sounded very worried. "My website isn't working, and some customer information is missing!" he said.

My mom is a cybersecurity analyst. Her job is to keep computers and information safe from attacks. She opened her laptop right away. While she was checking the website, I was sitting quietly next to her. She showed me some strange messages that came from another country.

"Someone tried to get into the website," Mom explained. "But don't worry. The information isn't lost. It was only hidden." She worked for two hours, and at eight o'clock the website was working again!

Later, Uncle Khalid sent us a video message. He said, "Thank you! You are the person who saved my business!"

After dinner, Mom told me about her friend Nouf. She is an AI specialist who designs programs with artificial intelligence. These programs can find attacks very fast. Maybe one day I will have a job like Mom's.

Lama

questions.prompt: What was Lama doing when Uncle Khalid called?
questions.explanation: Lama writes, "I was doing my math homework after school when Uncle Khalid called."

questions.prompt: What does Uncle Khalid's business sell?
questions.explanation: The diary says his business sells dates and coffee online.

questions.statement: Lama's mom keeps computers and information safe from attacks.
questions.explanation: She is a cybersecurity analyst, and her job is to keep computers and information safe from attacks.

questions.statement: The customer information was lost forever.
questions.explanation: Mom says, "The information isn't lost. It was only hidden."

questions.prompt: Nouf is an AI specialist ___ designs programs with artificial intelligence.
questions.explanation: The text says "an AI specialist who designs programs", and we use who for people.

questions.prompt: How did Uncle Khalid say thank you?
questions.explanation: The diary says Uncle Khalid sent them a video message to say thank you.

reading.title: Ten Minutes with an Astronaut
reading.text:
Last week, Captain Majed, a Saudi astronaut, visited our boys' school in Riyadh. Omar and Fahad from Grade 6 interviewed him for the school newsletter.

Omar: When did you first want to go to space?
Captain Majed: When I was ten, I was watching TV with my father when a rocket took off. I said, "One day, that will be me!"

Fahad: What was your job on the space station?
Captain Majed: I was part of a team that did science tests. For example, we grew small plants which can live without soil. We also checked a satellite that sends weather pictures to Earth.

Omar: What was the most exciting moment?
Captain Majed: One night, I was looking out of the window while the others were sleeping. Suddenly, I saw the lights of Jeddah and the Red Sea. Our planet looked so beautiful!

Fahad: Did you miss your family?
Captain Majed: Yes, very much. Every Friday, my children recorded a video message for me.

Omar: What is your advice for us?
Captain Majed: Study science and math, and never stop asking questions. The astronauts who will fly into space in the future are sitting in classrooms like yours today!

questions.prompt: What was Captain Majed doing when he saw a rocket take off?
questions.explanation: He says, "I was watching TV with my father when a rocket took off."

questions.statement: The plants on the space station grew in soil.
questions.explanation: The team grew small plants which can live without soil.

questions.statement: The satellite sends weather pictures to Earth.
questions.explanation: Captain Majed checked a satellite that sends weather pictures to Earth.

questions.prompt: What did he see from the window one night?
options: the lights of Jeddah and the Red Sea
questions.answer: the lights of Jeddah and the Red Sea
questions.explanation: He says he suddenly saw the lights of Jeddah and the Red Sea.

questions.prompt: Every Friday, his children recorded a ___ for him.
questions.explanation: He says his children recorded a video message for him every Friday.

questions.prompt: In "we grew small plants which can live without soil", what does which refer to?
questions.explanation: Which comes right after small plants and tells us which plants: plants are things, so we use which.

reading.title: Fast Help at the Bakery
reading.text:
JEDDAH, Saturday: Firefighters, police officers and paramedics worked together yesterday morning after a small fire started in a bakery on Palm Street.

At about seven o'clock, the bakers were making bread for the busy weekend when smoke came out of an old oven. One baker, Mr. Yasser, called the emergency number. "We were working fast, and suddenly the kitchen was full of smoke," he said.

The fire station is only two streets away, so the fire truck arrived in four minutes. The firefighters who came were quick and calm. They put out the fire in ten minutes. While they were working, two police officers closed the street and kept people away from the shop.

An ambulance came too. A young baker who was coughing went to the hospital, but he is fine now.

Later, a little girl was missing in the crowd, and her mother was very scared. A police officer found her near a juice shop and brought her back to her mother.

Mr. Yasser's business is going to open again next week. "I want to thank the people who helped us," he said. "They are real heroes."

questions.prompt: What were the bakers doing when the smoke came out of the oven?
questions.explanation: The report says the bakers were making bread when smoke came out of an old oven.

questions.statement: The fire truck arrived quickly because the fire station is near the bakery.
questions.explanation: The fire station is only two streets away, so the fire truck arrived in four minutes.

questions.statement: The police officers put out the fire.
questions.explanation: The firefighters put out the fire, and the police officers closed the street.

questions.prompt: Who went to the hospital?
options: a young baker who was coughing
questions.answer: a young baker who was coughing
questions.explanation: The report says a young baker who was coughing went to the hospital.

questions.prompt: A police officer found the missing girl near a ___.
questions.explanation: The report says a police officer found her near a juice shop.

questions.prompt: In "The firefighters who came were quick and calm", why does the writer use who?
questions.explanation: We use who for people, so the text says the firefighters who came.

wordWork.title: Open and closed compound nouns
wordWork.rule: A compound noun is two words joined to make a new noun. Closed compounds are written as one word (firefighter), and open compounds are written as two words (fire truck).

items.prompt: fire + fighter = ___ (one word)
items.explanation: Firefighter is a closed compound: we write it as one word.

items.prompt: police + station = ___ (two words)
items.explanation: Police station is an open compound: we write two words.

items.prompt: Which is a closed compound noun?
items.explanation: Firefighter is one word, so it is closed. The others are two words.

items.prompt: Which is an open compound noun?
items.explanation: Video message is written as two words, so it is open.

items.prompt: Which compound noun is a person?
items.explanation: The second word, officer, tells us it is a person.

items.prompt: A ___ is a person who guards swimmers at the beach. (life + guard)
items.explanation: Life + guard makes the closed compound lifeguard.

items.prompt: A ___ is a place where you buy books. (book + store)
items.explanation: Book + store makes the closed compound bookstore.

items.prompt: What is a fire station?
items.explanation: The second word, station, tells us it is a place.

items.prompt: A ___ is a vest that keeps you safe in the water. (life + jacket)
items.explanation: Life jacket is an open compound: two words.

writing.prompt: Write about an exciting or unusual message you got or sent. What happened?
writing.hint: Use the Simple Past and Past Progressive with when / while. Say how you felt.
writing.model: Last summer, my family was traveling to AlUla. We were driving through the desert when my phone beeped. It was a video message from my cousin Sara. She was standing in front of a rocket at a space museum! She said, "I'm going to be an astronaut one day!" I felt very happy for her, so I sent her a message back.

writing.prompt: Describe a job that helps people. Who does it, and why is it important?
writing.hint: Use who / which / that. Use words like ambulance, police officer, firefighter.
writing.model: A paramedic is a person who helps sick or hurt people. Paramedics drive an ambulance which has special machines inside. They often work at night. I think it is an important job because paramedics save lives. My neighbor is a paramedic who works in Riyadh, and she is very brave and kind.

speaking: An astronaut is a person who travels into space.
Sara was traveling to AlUla when she recorded her video message.
The firefighter who climbed the tree saved the kitten.
A satellite is a machine which goes around Earth.
I was doing my homework when the phone rang.
My uncle is a robotics engineer who designs robots.
The ambulance arrived while the police officer was helping the man.
Every job is important, so we should thank the people who help us.
